title: Midnight at the Lumen Museum
brief: At the Lumen Museum gala, a planned ninety-second blackout began at 10:00 p.m. When the lights returned, Aurora Circuit was missing from its display. The secured wing remained closed until the initial investigation began. Four people had relevant access, knowledge, or equipment: curator Mara Vale, lighting technician Theo Quinn, security lead Nia Brooks, and catalog photographer Rowan Pike.

suspects.name: Mara Vale
suspects.public_profile: Mara uses she/her pronouns. She approved the catalog shoot and the display case's temporary calibration mode. The exhibition is the centerpiece of her season.

suspects.name: Theo Quinn
suspects.public_profile: Theo uses he/him pronouns. He designed the gala lighting sequence and maintains the console that triggered the blackout cue.

suspects.name: Nia Brooks
suspects.public_profile: Nia uses she/her pronouns. She controls the wing's security procedures, supervises equipment screening, and carries master access.

suspects.name: Rowan Pike
suspects.public_profile: Rowan uses he/him pronouns. He photographed Aurora Circuit before the gala and brought a hard equipment case into the secured wing.

locations.name: Gallery 3 display case
locations.description: The smart-glass case, its rear service panel, and the instrumented plinth.

locations.name: Media locker
locations.description: The secure locker holding checked camera gear and removable media.

locations.name: Security screening station
locations.description: The station that records incoming gear and media-locker intake weights.

locations.name: Lighting booth
locations.description: The isolated control room containing the cue console and input audit log.

observations.title: The plinth lost its load before the blackout
observations.text: Plinth W-3 recorded a stable net load of 1.84 kilograms until 9:42:18 p.m., when it fell to 0.00 kilograms. It stayed at 0.00 throughout the 10:00 p.m. blackout, and a post-incident self-test passed.

observations.title: The service-panel contact was bypassed
observations.text: The case entered approved calibration mode at 9:39:04 p.m. From 9:42:11 to 9:42:24, the hinge reported open while the magnetic contact reported closed. Inspectors recovered a square of matte gaffer tape over that contact.

observations.title: A polarized image insert masked the empty case
observations.text: Inspectors found a polarized acetate insert in the front guide. From the marked gala viewing line, it displayed a convincing image of Aurora Circuit. Its crop matches a catalog image available in the shared press folder.

observations.title: Rowan had exclusive gallery access at 9:42 p.m.
observations.text: An occupancy sweep marked Gallery 3 empty at 9:37:40 p.m. Rowan entered at 9:39:04 under work order G3-CAT-17. No other person entered before Rowan exited at 9:45:11.

observations.title: Rowan denied approaching the case
observations.text: Rowan stated: 'I stayed behind the brass line the whole shoot. The nearest I got was about three meters, and I never touched the case.'

observations.title: Rowan's camera was beside the open service panel
observations.text: Frame RP_2207 on Rowan's camera card was captured at 9:42:07 p.m. Its calibrated focus distance is 0.55 meters, and the case's rear service panel is visibly ajar in the frame reflection.

observations.title: Rowan's hard case gained exactly 1.84 kilograms
observations.text: Rowan's hard case weighed 7.92 kilograms at entry and 9.76 kilograms at media-locker intake, a gain of exactly 1.84 kilograms. His equipment manifest records no added gear, and corridor footage shows no handoff.

observations.title: The blackout cue ran automatically
observations.text: Cue BLACKOUT_90 was loaded earlier that afternoon and executed automatically at 10:00 p.m. The console audit records no manual input from 9:55 to 10:02 p.m.

observations.title: Three suspects were independently elsewhere at 9:42 p.m.
observations.text: At 9:42:18 p.m., Mara is continuously visible on the greenroom rehearsal feed, Theo is visible inside the lighting booth, and Nia's body camera records her sealing a delivery at the loading bay. Rowan is the only suspect recorded in Gallery 3.

timeline_events.summary: Plinth W-3 loses the artwork's full 1.84-kilogram net load.
The preloaded BLACKOUT_90 cue runs automatically.
Rowan is the sole recorded occupant of Gallery 3.
Mara remains visible on the continuous greenroom rehearsal feed.
Theo remains visible inside the lighting booth.
Nia's body camera records an uninterrupted loading-bay seal check.
Rowan's hard case weighs 7.92 kilograms at museum entry.
Rowan's hard case weighs 9.76 kilograms at media-locker intake.

reveal_routes.summary: The display case yields three source-backed observations about timing and concealment.
The checked camera card contains a close-range frame from the critical minute.
Security records allow the same hard case to be compared at two checkpoints.
The console audit distinguishes an automatic cue from manual activity.
Mara says she was on the continuous greenroom rehearsal feed during the catalog shoot and asks investigators to verify it.
Mara confirms that she approved calibration mode for the catalog shoot, which temporarily disengaged the motor lock for filter adjustment.
Theo says he remained in the isolated lighting booth during the relevant setup window and points investigators to its interior camera.
Theo says BLACKOUT_90 was a scheduled automatic cue and suggests checking the console audit rather than accepting his statement.
Nia says her body camera recorded her sealing a delivery at the loading bay during the catalog shoot.
Nia explains that hard equipment cases are weighed both at entry and when checked into the media locker.
Rowan gives a definite account of how close he came to the artwork.
Rowan says his hard case held only the equipment listed on his entry manifest and that its contents did not change.
Correlating the plinth event with access control and independent recordings isolates the actual 9:42 p.m. opportunity window.
Comparing the blackout with the plinth log shows that discovery and removal occurred at different times.
